statements.context: e with the Go-Live of its Federal Electronic Health Record. VA Deputy Secretary Paul R. Lawrence, PhD, visited the Marion and Fort Wayne VA Medical Centers Aug. 20-21, meeting with VANIHCS senior leaders, the change leadership team, and front-line staff to recognize their dedication and discuss the impact of the transition to the new electronic health record platform. Lawrence’s visit underscored the significance of the Indiana market’s Go-Live milestone, part of a nationwide implementation designed to improve both Veterans’ experiences and provider access to information. “I’m thrilled to be here with you in Indiana for this historic Go-Live,” said Lawrence. “The energy, teamwork, and commitment I’ve seen among the staff here at VA Northern Indiana is truly inspiring. This is a tremendous step forward for Veterans’ care, and it’s possible because of your dedication.” During his two-day tour, Lawrence met with staff at the Marion VA Medical Center, visiting the EHRM Incident Command Center, outpatient mental health clinic, and Eagle’s Wing Community Living Center. He concluded his Marion visit by joining a Go-Live celebration in the medical center’s atrium, where he applauded team members’ tireless preparations. That evening, Lawrence participated in a Veteran Roundtable at VFW Post 857 in Fort Wayne. Veterans shared their concerns and hopes regarding the transition, while Lawrence and leaders from the Veterans Health Administration, the Veterans Benefits Administration, and local organizations addressed questions about the system’s features and advantages. “It’s a great new system that will help serve you better since you will no longer have to worry about access to your records when traveling to other parts of the country,” Lawrence explained to attendees. “Someday your records will be there waiting for you at other VAs, wherever you might go.” On the morning of Aug. 21, Lawrence appeared live on Fort Wayne’s 21 Alive television morning show, where he described the benefits Veterans will experience as VA modernizes its health care technology. “We have the best doctors with us, now we will have the best tools to use with all the information to provide even better care,” he said. “This new electronic health records system is the tool the private sector is using,” Lawrence added. “Now the VA is using it.
